recent_posts.title: Crafting over Comparing | Start a Mini Learning Project
recent_posts.summary: A framework for starting week-long mini learning projects to rekindle curiosity and combat learning fatigue. The approach involves creating a knowledge map of what you already know, identifying gaps, finding quality review papers and lectures, and producing tangible outputs like notebooks or articles. The method emphasizes low-stakes exploration, daily habit formation, and metacognitive reflection on personal learning preferences rather than perfectionism.

recent_posts.title: How to Research Any Topic - Deep-Dive like a PhD Student
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to conducting deep research like a PhD student, covering the entire process from formulating specific research questions to building knowledge networks. The methodology includes starting with review papers, using citation mapping tools like Research Rabbit and reference managers like Zotero, critically evaluating sources for biases and limitations, and documenting findings in a structured system. Emphasis is placed on active learning through creating outputs like essays or blog posts, maintaining daily research logs, and building momentum through consistent practice and question-driven exploration.

recent_posts.title: Attention over Distraction - Improve your Focus through Deep Research
recent_posts.summary: Explores how researchers develop deep focus through sustained engagement with difficult problems, and how anyone can train this skill. Discusses the difference between reactive and intentional attention, recommends practicing with challenging books, and introduces concepts from Deep Work and flow states. Emphasizes that focus is a trainable skill requiring deliberate practice, noting how modern technology competes for our attention while dedicated reading and mindfulness can help reclaim it.

recent_posts.title: How to build a self directed learning curriculum like a PhD student
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to self-directed learning using PhD-level research methodologies. Covers creating custom learning curricula, building knowledge systems through 'intellectual gardening' (weeding outdated info, cross-pollinating ideas, composting notes), and using tools like Notion and reference managers. Emphasizes starting with a clear 'why', breaking topics into fundamentals, finding or creating syllabi, active reading with opposing viewpoints, and balancing structured systems with playful obsession. Includes practical examples from computational psychiatry ethics research.

recent_posts.title: Creating over Consuming - Using One Scientific Notebook
recent_posts.summary: A PhD student shares their scientific notebook method for shifting from consumption to creation mindset. The approach combines timestamp journaling (interstitial journaling) to track time and thoughts, weekly audits to identify patterns, and strategies to balance creating versus consuming content. Key practices include noting task switches, tracking distractions and ideas, recording emotional blocks, and starting days with creative work rather than reading. The method helps maintain focus on large, ambiguous academic projects while building awareness of time allocation between productive creation and passive consumption.

recent_posts.title: Academic reading techniques for better retention and consistent habits
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to developing effective reading habits using academic techniques. Covers two main reading approaches: purpose-driven reading for specific questions and inquisitive reading for curiosity. Emphasizes retention strategies like encountering ideas in multiple formats, integration through writing and discussion, and tracking personal growth through rereading highlighted passages. Provides practical tips for reading multiple books simultaneously, making reading a default activity instead of phone scrolling, and balancing different difficulty levels to maintain engagement.

recent_posts.title: Structure Over Chaos | How to Self-Learn Like a PhD Student
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses how to approach self-learning like a PhD student, emphasizing the importance of setting clear goals, curating resources, and maintaining motivation. It lays out a structured process for goal setting, finding relevant learning materials, and creating a self-learning schedule to stay consistent. Additionally, it explores tools and strategies to track progress and apply knowledge actively.

recent_posts.title: Discovery over Content Consuming | Working like a Scientist
recent_posts.summary: The post highlights the importance of curiosity, uncertainty, and experimentation in fostering knowledge and creativity, particularly through the scientific process. It emphasizes how schooling rewards perfection while real-life learning and achievements stem from exploring and challenging unknowns. The author shares personal experiences from their PhD journey, advocating for curiosity-driven learning and providing practical advice on engaging with scientific research and building supportive environments.

recent_posts.title: Observation over Distraction | Write like a PhD Student
recent_posts.summary: Explore the importance of cultivating writing as a habit, regardless of fancy tools or pressure. Learn techniques to overcome challenges such as self-doubt, and perfectionism. Embrace short-term and long-term writing projects to maintain motivation. Discover writing strategies like morning pages and reverse outlining to improve writing structure and flow. Protect writing time from distractions, use small time pockets for creativity, and focus on consistency over perfection to enhance writing skills.

recent_posts.title: Questions over Assumptions | Note-Taking like a PhD student
recent_posts.summary: The post explores effective note-taking strategies, emphasizing the importance of organizing and connecting ideas to enhance learning and creativity. It introduces the Zettelkasten-inspired framework, highlighting its benefits in forming a web of interconnected knowledge. The author shares personal experiences using digital tools such as Notion, alongside recommendations for mindful consumption and reflection. The goal is to utilize notes to generate new insights and foster continuous learning.
